claims.text: Introducing stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations into tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys will simultaneously improve strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance.
The initial as-cast alloy has a single-phase BCC microstructure with minimal secondary phases.
Controlled high-temperature annealing can induce stepwise formation of coherent nanoprecipitates in the alloy matrix.
Moderate heating and stepwise cooling prevent rapid quenching and the formation of large, incoherent precipitates.
The treatment should work in tungsten-based refractory HEAs whose thermodynamics favor coherent nanoprecipitate nucleation.
The structural mediator consists of coherent nanoscale precipitates within a BCC matrix.
The coherent nanoprecipitates may be carbides or intermetallic phases.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve localized stress concentrations that can cause premature crack initiation.
SCCPs can overcome the conventional strength–ductility trade-off.
Coherent nanoprecipitates increase the alloy’s effective Young’s modulus.
Coherent nanoprecipitates improve fracture toughness by limiting crack initiation and propagation.
An SCCP-containing tungsten refractory HEA can attain an ultrahigh strength of approximately 2.15 GPa.
An SCCP-containing tungsten refractory HEA can attain approximately 15% tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
The treatment will increase both tensile and compressive strength relative to an untreated refractory HEA.
The treatment will improve Young’s modulus relative to an untreated refractory HEA.
The treatment will enhance resistance to crack propagation relative to an untreated refractory HEA.
Conventionally processed refractory HEAs typically exhibit a trade-off between high strength and tensile ductility.
Conventionally processed refractory HEAs have lower fracture resistance and modulus because they lack controlled secondary-phase formation.
Rapidly quenched alloys or compositions unable to form coherent interfaces may fail to show the predicted improvements.
